catalog_quote: Inventaire. Il existe comme en lingála deux tons de base (bas et haut) avec possibilité de combinaison pour engendrer des tons doubles (descendant et montant). Le ton bas est ici représenté par l’absence de tout signe. Les tons haut, descendant et montant sont marqués respectivement par l’accent aigu, l’accent circonflexe normal et l’accent circonflexe renversé. [...] Les tons ont une valeur aussi bien lexicale que grammaticale. [...] Règles tonales. Les principales règles tonales sont: la contraction, la neutralisation, l’harmonie, le contraste, la métatonie et la faille tonale.

new_statements.translation: Inventory. As in Lingala there are two basic tones (low and high), which can combine to produce double tones (falling and rising). Low tone is represented here by the absence of any mark; high, falling and rising tones are marked respectively by the acute accent, the ordinary circumflex and the inverted circumflex. [...] Tones have both lexical and grammatical value. [...] Tone rules. The main tone rules are contraction, neutralisation, harmony, contrast, metatony and tonal downstep ('faille').

new_statements.rule_in_words: Mbenga (Mbinga dialect of Mabaale) is described as a two-tone (H/L, with HL and LH contours) Bantu language with lexically and grammatically distinctive tone; the sketch gives tone rules but makes no statement at all about word stress or accent, so no stress position can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None concerning stress; tonal phenomena only (metatony: final -a of the infinitive lowers its H phrase-finally; H of a word-final syllable may spread to the first syllable of the next word after elision).
new_statements.domain_note: Word- and phrase-level tone; vowel length said not to be distinctive ('on ne peut pas parler de longueur vocalique proprement dite', p.17) apart from lengthening under vowel contraction. No penultimate-lengthening or prominence remark.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes Mbenga of Mankanza (Nouvel-Anvers), which Glottolog's bibliography note equates with the Mbinga dialect [mbin1238] of Mabaale [maba1270]; the authors themselves treat 'mabale' (spoken at Bonginda, Bobelu, Bokolongela, Mabembe etc.) as a neighbouring, closely related lect. The 1990 volume's relevant sketch is of Balobo (= Lobo dialect [lobo1240]). The language-level Mabale-de-Mankanza variety is described only in Motingea 1996 (Afrika und Ubersee 79), not accessible online.

sources.note: Sec. 2.1 'Phonetique et phonologie' pp.15-27 read; sec. 2.1.3 'Tons' pp.22-26: two basic tones (low, high) plus falling/rising contours, tones have lexical and grammatical value, tone rules (contraction, neutralisation/spreading, faille, harmony, contrast, metatony). Vowel sequences from consonant loss, 'on ne peut pas parler de longueur vocalique proprement dite' (p.17). No statement about stress or accent anywhere in the work (the only occurrences of 'accent' are diacritic names, p.22). Describes Mbenga of Mankanza, which Glottolog equates with the Mbinga dialect [mbin1238] of Mabaale.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1951. La tonologie des parlers bantous du nord-ouest du Congo belge. Bulletin des Seances, Institut Royal Colonial Belge 22(4): 900-919.
sources.note: Areal tone typology (type lingala vs. 'tonologie deplacee' of the Bangala-des-marais, Budza, Doko, Dzamba types); riverine peoples of the Ubangi, Congo and Ngiri ('Bangala-des-grandes-eaux') have lingala-type tonology. No accent/stress statement; Mabale not named individually. Cited by Motingea & Bonzoi 2008 for 'tons doubles courts'.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu. 1990. Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaire: elements de structure grammaticale (Etudes Aequatoria 8). Bamanya (Mbandaka): Centre Aequatoria. 284 pp.
sources.note: Libinza sub-group list (p.221) names Mabembe, Ewaku (Litoka), Mabale (de Mankanza), Bondongo-Libinza, Balobo, Ndobo, but this volume sketches only Litoka, Balobo and Ndobo; no Mabale-de-Mankanza sketch. Balobo (= Lobo dialect [lobo1240] of Mabaale per Glottolog) phonology p.239-240: 7 vowels, consonant notes, and only 'La tonologie est comparativement au Bantu commun du type normal'; nothing on accent/stress. General introduction has no accent remarks.
